evidence: Noosa Northshore Ferries – River Conditions Update Following the recent heavy rainfall across the region and the Minor Flood Warning for the Noosa River, conditions in the area are now beginning to improve. At this stage, it appears we have moved through the worst of the flooding, and river levels are expected to continue returning to safer operating conditions from today onwards. Our team will continue to closely monitor river levels, tides, and weather conditions; however ferry services are currently operating as normal between Tewantin and Noosa Northshore. Due to elevated river levels, ferry ramps remain steeper than usual. Customers travelling in buses, motorhomes, lowered vehicles, or vehicles towing trailers are asked to take extra care when boarding and disembarking the ferry, and to follow all instructions from our deck crew to ensure safe loading and unloading. — Noosa Northsho
connector_name: Noosa North Shore Ferry graph connector

connector_policy.CLOSED: The ferry is still reported CLOSED, but the released graph does not contain a usable Cooloola fallback path. To prevent false full isolation, the crossing is represented as a conditional-access proxy for the published 4WD alternative; the proxy is available in impassable-only analysis and blocked in all-blocking analysis.
connector_policy.UNKNOWN: No ferry closure is injected; topology fails open to avoid false isolation, while the dashboard reports UNKNOWN.

four_wd_fallback.model_policy: If the ferry closes, use a conditional-access proxy rather than falsely declaring full isolation because the graph omitted the published 4WD alternative.
four_wd_fallback.access: High-clearance 4WD only; vehicle access permit and beach/tide/park conditions apply.

topology_check.reason: Released graph does not contain a ferry-independent path between Third Cutting and Rainbow Beach; conditional proxy will be used if the ferry closes.
